degree to which the claim depends on formal definitions, derivation, or proof
dependence on observational rather than intervention evidence
dependence on controlled or intervention evidence
dependence on computation, simulation, or executable analysis
dependence on chronology, archival evidence, or past-state reconstruction
degree of ought, policy, ethical, or prescriptive content
degree of interpretive or hermeneutic judgement
strength of causal rather than associational claim
degree of future-state or unseen-state prediction
degree of descriptive factual content
degree of recommendation, instruction, or required action
specificity to a named or individual case
degree of population, aggregate, or group-level inference
dependence on a legal or regulatory jurisdiction

declared unresolved uncertainty
strength and directness of evidence supporting the claim

hard_constraints.meaning: a binding legal claim cannot be represented as strongly authoritative when its legal authority or provenance is weak
clinical guidance cannot be structurally supported only by weak or preliminary evidence
high-consequence low-evidence claims must carry high uncertainty rather than confident presentation
material cross-domain dependence requires an explicit bridge

consumer_rule: if a vector violates a hard constraint, return MODE_VIOLATION or weaken the claim; never repair a violation by inventing stronger evidence
